catalog.title: UNCONSCIOUS ADULT
catalog.blurb: A dialogue-driven rescue on 8th Street. Speak, assign tasks, and decide. No running — only communication.

unconscious-adult.title: UNCONSCIOUS ADULT
unconscious-adult.subtitle: Training conversation — not a substitute for a certified CPR course.
learningPoints: Make the scene safe before you help — do not run into traffic.
Tap the shoulders and shout. Do not shake hard.
Point at a specific person to call emergency services and return when connected. Send another person for an AED.
Check breathing for no more than 10 seconds. Gasping is not normal breathing.
If unresponsive and not breathing normally, start CPR right away. Do not wait for the AED.
Stay with the dispatcher. Use the AED on a bare chest and follow the prompts. Keep CPR going until told to pause.

scene_safe.title: SCENE SAFETY
scene_safe.hint: Look for traffic, fire, or wires. Speak up: wait until it is safe, then approach.
scene_safe.hintQuestion: In this training scene, why must the hero say the street is unsafe before anyone runs to the collapsed adult?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: Dusk on 8th Street. Neon buzzes. An adult lies still near the curb. Cars still roll.

lines.speaker: RICK
lines.text: Someone's down! Come on — we gotta run over there NOW!

lines.speaker: MAYA
lines.text: I don't know... those cars aren't stopping.

lines.speaker: COACH PULSE
lines.text: Hero. Before anyone moves — what do you SAY first?

choices.label: "Hold it! Check the street first. We only go when it's safe."
choices.playerLine: Hold it! Look both ways. We don't run into traffic. When the street is clear, THEN we approach.

reply.speaker: RICK
reply.text: Yeah... yeah. I almost stepped off the curb.

reply.speaker: MAYA
reply.text: Gap in the cars. Sidewalk's okay. Let's go.

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Correct. You cannot help if you become the next patient.

choices.label: "There's no time — sprint into the street!"
choices.playerLine: There's no time! I'm going in!

reply.speaker: NARRATOR
reply.text: A horn blasts. Tires scream. A car swerves.

reply.speaker: RICK
reply.text: HEY! That car almost took you out!

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Unsafe. Running into live traffic can make a second victim. Say it: wait, look, then approach.

choices.label: "Forget looking — start chest compressions in the road!"
choices.playerLine: Forget looking around — start compressions right here in the street!

reply.speaker: MAYA
reply.text: In the LANE? We'll all get hit!

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Not yet. You have not checked safety, response, or breathing. CPR comes after those words and those checks.

choices.label: "Not our problem. Keep walking."
choices.playerLine: Someone else will deal with it. Let's go.

reply.speaker: MAYA
reply.text: They're not moving, though...

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Unsafe. If the scene can be made safe, you stay, you speak, and you get help. Walking away delays care.

check_response.title: CHECK RESPONSE
check_response.hint: Kneel. Tap both shoulders. Shout. Watch the face. Do not shake.
check_response.hintQuestion: What should the hero say and do to check if a collapsed adult responds, without shaking them?

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: You kneel on the sidewalk. The adult is still. Neon paints their face.

lines.speaker: RICK
lines.text: Are they... sleeping? Should I shake 'em?

lines.speaker: COACH PULSE
lines.text: Your words matter. How do you check if they respond?

choices.label: Tap the shoulders and shout: "Are you okay? Can you hear me?"
choices.playerLine: I'm tapping the shoulders — ARE YOU OKAY? CAN YOU HEAR ME?

reply.speaker: NARRATOR
reply.text: No words. No eye opening. No movement toward your voice.

reply.speaker: MAYA
reply.text: Nothing. That's bad, right?

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: No response. Emergency. Next: point at people and assign help.

choices.label: "Wake up!" — shake them hard
choices.playerLine: WAKE UP! *shakes hard*

reply.speaker: RICK
reply.text: Whoa, easy! You could hurt their neck!

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Unsafe. Hard shaking can cause injury. Tap the shoulders and shout. Try that line.

choices.label: "Maya, splash water on their face!"
choices.playerLine: Maya, grab a bottle — splash their face!

reply.speaker: MAYA
reply.text: I... I don't think that's how this works.

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: That is not a response check and can cause harm. Tap and shout. No water.

choices.label: "Give them two minutes. Maybe they'll sit up."
choices.playerLine: Let's wait a couple minutes. Maybe they'll wake up.

reply.speaker: RICK
reply.text: Two minutes of just standing here?!

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Waiting wastes time. If they do not respond now, you assign help now.

assign_help.title: ASSIGN HELP
assign_help.hint: Point at one person for the call. Point at another for the AED. Tell the caller to come back when connected.
assign_help.hintQuestion: Why should the hero point at a specific bystander to call emergency services and return when connected, and send another for an AED?

lines.speaker: RICK
lines.text: Tell us what to do! I have a phone!

lines.speaker: MAYA
lines.text: There's a building lobby behind us. I can run.

lines.speaker: COACH PULSE
lines.text: Don't say 'somebody.' Point. Give each person one job.

choices.label: "Rick, call emergency services and come back when you're connected. Maya, get an AED!"
choices.playerLine: Rick — call emergency services and return to tell me when you've connected. Maya — get an AED and bring it here!

reply.speaker: RICK
reply.text: Got it! Calling now — I'll shout when they pick up!

reply.speaker: MAYA
reply.text: AED. On it. Don't leave them.

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: That's how you activate help. Stay with the patient.

choices.label: "I'll go hunt for an AED. You two wait."
choices.playerLine: I'll go find an AED myself. You two just... wait here with them.

reply.speaker: RICK
reply.text: You're leaving us with someone who isn't answering?!

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Unsafe. Do not abandon them for a long search. Send Maya. You stay. Rick calls.

choices.label: "Someone should call... whenever."
choices.playerLine: Uh, somebody should probably call, I guess.

reply.speaker: MAYA
reply.text: Somebody who? We're looking at YOU.

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Vague words waste seconds. Point: 'YOU — call, then come back when connected.'

choices.label: "Help me load them in a car. We'll drive."
choices.playerLine: Grab their legs. We'll drive them to the hospital!

reply.speaker: RICK
reply.text: I can't drive AND you can't do CPR in a back seat like that!

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Unsafe. Bring help here. You cannot drive and give CPR. Call, AED, stay.

phone_connect.title: DISPATCHER
phone_connect.hint: Keep Rick on speaker. Tell dispatch the adult is unresponsive. Then check breathing.

lines.speaker: RICK
lines.text: They're CONNECTED! I'm putting it on speaker!

lines.speaker: DISPATCH
lines.text: Emergency. What's the exact location and what's happening?

lines.speaker: YOU
lines.text: 8th Street sidewalk. Adult collapsed. Not responding. We're with them.

lines.speaker: DISPATCH
lines.text: Stay on the line. Is the person breathing normally? Look at the chest.

lines.speaker: COACH PULSE
lines.text: Dispatcher is coaching you. Next words: a fast breathing check — ten seconds, not a minute.

check_breathing.title: CHECK BREATHING
check_breathing.hint: Look, listen, feel — no more than 10 seconds. Occasional gasping is NOT normal breathing.
check_breathing.hintQuestion: Why is a 10-second breathing check required, and why is gasping not treated as normal breathing?

lines.speaker: DISPATCH
lines.text: Look at the chest. Tell me if you see normal breathing.

lines.speaker: NARRATOR
lines.text: The chest is still... then a strange isolated gasp.

lines.speaker: RICK
lines.text: They gasped! That means they're okay, right?

lines.speaker: COACH PULSE
lines.text: Answer carefully. What do you tell Rick and Dispatch?

choices.label: "Ten seconds: look, listen, feel. That gasp is NOT normal breathing."
choices.playerLine: Looking ten seconds — look, listen, feel. That gasp is NOT normal breathing. Unresponsive, not breathing normally.

reply.speaker: DISPATCH
reply.text: Copy. If they are unresponsive and not breathing normally, start CPR. I'll stay with you.

reply.speaker: RICK
reply.text: So the gasp wasn't 'okay'...

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Correct. Agonal gasps are a reason to start CPR, not to wait.

choices.label: "Dispatch, I'm going to watch for a full minute to be sure."
choices.playerLine: I'll watch for a whole minute to be extra sure.

reply.speaker: DISPATCH
reply.text: Do not wait a minute. A breathing check is about ten seconds.

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Too slow. Long watching is a dangerous delay. Ten seconds, then act.

choices.label: "They gasped, so they're breathing. We wait."
choices.playerLine: They gasped once, so they're breathing. We can wait.

reply.speaker: DISPATCH
reply.text: Isolated gasping is not normal breathing. Treat it like no breathing.

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Unsafe. Gasping can happen when the heart has stopped. Do not wait.

choices.label: "Roll them on their side and wait."
choices.playerLine: Recovery position. Roll them on their side.

reply.speaker: DISPATCH
reply.text: Not if they are not breathing normally. They need CPR on their back.

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Unsafe here. Recovery position is for unresponsive AND breathing normally.

start_cpr.title: BEGIN CPR
start_cpr.hint: Start compressions now, center of the chest. Do not wait for Maya's AED.
start_cpr.hintQuestion: If the adult is unresponsive and not breathing normally, why must the hero start CPR before the AED arrives?

lines.speaker: DISPATCH
lines.text: Hands on the center of the chest. Push hard and fast. Count out loud.

lines.speaker: RICK
lines.text: Maya isn't back with the box yet... do we wait?

lines.speaker: COACH PULSE
lines.text: Speak the decision. Waiting without compressions means no blood flow.

choices.label: "Starting CPR now. Center of the chest. Hard and fast."
choices.playerLine: I'm starting CPR now — hands in the center of the chest, hard and fast. Rick, keep Dispatch on speaker!

reply.speaker: DISPATCH
reply.text: Good. Keep going. Let the chest come all the way up between pushes.

reply.speaker: NARRATOR
reply.text: You compress on a firm sidewalk. Count in rhythm.

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Correct. 100 to 120 a minute. This game's rhythm is 110. Don't stop for the box.

choices.label: "We wait for the AED. No compressions until then."
choices.playerLine: We'll wait for the AED. No compressions until Maya's back.

reply.speaker: DISPATCH
reply.text: Start CPR now. Use the AED the moment it arrives — don't wait to push.

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Unsafe. No compressions means no blood flow. Start now.

choices.label: "I'll only give breaths. No chest pushes."
choices.playerLine: I'll just give breaths. Skipping the chest.

reply.speaker: DISPATCH
reply.text: Chest compressions are the priority. Do not skip them.

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: For a collapsed adult, push. Breaths can be added if trained — never instead of compressions.

choices.label: "Sit them up so they can breathe."
choices.playerLine: Help me sit them up. Maybe they'll breathe easier.

reply.speaker: RICK
reply.text: They're dead weight — this isn't helping!

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Unsafe. They need a firm flat back for CPR, not sitting.

aed_dispatcher.title: AED + DISPATCH
aed_dispatcher.hint: Keep CPR. Turn the AED on. Bare chest. Follow voice prompts. Stay on the line.
aed_dispatcher.hintQuestion: When the AED arrives, what should the hero tell Maya and Dispatch to do?

lines.speaker: MAYA
lines.text: GOT IT! Yellow box — what do I do?!

lines.speaker: DISPATCH
lines.text: Turn it on. Bare the chest. Follow the pictures. Keep CPR until it says to stop.

lines.speaker: COACH PULSE
lines.text: Last decision. Your line to Maya.

choices.label: "Keep CPR. Maya, power it on, pads on bare skin, follow the voice."
choices.playerLine: Keep compressions until it talks. Maya — turn it on, pads on BARE skin, follow the voice prompts. Dispatch, stay with us!

reply.speaker: AED
reply.text: ANALYZING. STAND CLEAR.

reply.speaker: YOU
reply.text: Clear! ... Shock delivered. Back on the chest!

reply.speaker: DISPATCH
reply.text: Units are pulling up. Keep CPR until they take over.

reply.speaker: NARRATOR
reply.text: Sirens wash the neon red. Paramedics kneel in. You did the talking that got help here.

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Training complete. Review the log. This was practice — take a real CPR course.

choices.label: "Stop everything. The ambulance is close enough."
choices.playerLine: Stop CPR. Help is close. We wait.

reply.speaker: DISPATCH
reply.text: Do not stop. Continue until the AED tells you to pause or crews take over.

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Unsafe. Close is not here. Compressions still matter.

choices.label: "Rick, hang up. I need to focus."
choices.playerLine: Rick, hang up on Dispatch. I need quiet.

reply.speaker: DISPATCH
reply.text: Stay on the line if you can. I can still coach the AED steps.

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Keep speakerphone. Dispatchers send the right help and talk you through.

choices.label: "Stick the pads on over the coat. Faster!"
choices.playerLine: Just slap the pads on over the coat — faster!

reply.speaker: MAYA
reply.text: The picture on the pad is a bare chest...

reply.speaker: DISPATCH
reply.text: Expose the chest. Pads on skin. Then analyze.

reply.speaker: COACH PULSE
reply.text: Pads on bare skin. Then stand clear when it says analyzing.
